explanation: Fill positions from right to left. At position i, choose an index uniformly from 0 through i with the supplied random source and swap that occurrence into position i.
correctness: Before an iteration, the unfilled prefix contains exactly the remaining occurrences. Each has probability 1/(i+1) of entering position i. Later swaps only touch earlier positions, so the filled suffix is final. Multiplying these conditional probabilities gives 1/n! for every occurrence permutation.
walkthrough: Start with [4,8,1]. At i=2, a supplied draw of 0 swaps the final occurrence with index 0, giving [1,8,4]. At i=1, a draw of 0 then gives [8,1,4]. Those choices have probability (1/3)*(1/2)=1/6. The actual draws may produce any of the six equally likely permutations; true denotes the judge validating distribution, multiplicities and mutation of the supplied array.
